data.narrative:
Standard Electron operates in the Climate & Energy sector at stealth stage. The valuation universe comprises nine peers: one public company (Lnza) and eight private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the peer set lacks sufficient homogeneity for conventional comparable-company analysis.

The peer-median method is not applicable due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables. Within the Climate & Energy sector, no same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers exist in sufficient quantity (minimum three required). While nine same-sector peers are identifiable, restricting the analysis to stealth-stage companies or valuation-tier alignment yields zero datapoints. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias given the heterogeneity of business models, technology maturity, and capital intensity across Climate & Energy subsectors.

Given these constraints, traditional triangulation cannot be completed. A defensible valuation requires either (1) expansion of comparable-stage or comparable-subsector data, (2) first-principles analysis of capital requirements and technology risk, or (3) delay pending additional disclosure of the company's specific technology, customer traction, or capital raised. The scarcity of stealth-stage Climate & Energy comparables reflects both sector concentration and the confidentiality typical of early-stage deep-tech. Any valuation estimate at this stage would rest on assumptions rather than market-observable data.
